$$(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^2 = 2 + 2\sqrt6 + 3 = 5+2\sqrt6.$$

Then multiply by $(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)$ again:
$$(5+2\sqrt6)(\sqrt2+\sqrt3) = 5\sqrt2 + 5\sqrt3 + 2\sqrt{12} + 2\sqrt{18}.$$

Simplify the radicals: $2\sqrt{12} = 4\sqrt3$ and $2\sqrt{18} = 6\sqrt2$. This gives
$$5\sqrt2 + 5\sqrt3 + 4\sqrt3 + 6\sqrt2 = 11\sqrt2 + 9\sqrt3.$$

So $a=11$, $b=9$, $c=0$, and $a+b+c = 20$.
